headline: B2B SaaS and Professional Services Case Studies
keyNotes: Even if people are already looking for your company by name, making smart changes to your online ads can dramatically cut costs, like one company that saw a 77% lower cost for each person who signed up for a trial.

When a company combined ads on Google Search with testing different versions of their website pages, they saw four times more good potential customers (called "qualified leads") and a 40% increase in their monthly income.

For a new product, advertising on social media platforms like LinkedIn and Meta can quickly generate many interested people, like the 130 trial registrations and demo requests one company received in just three months.

Using Google Search ads can create a lot of potential new business, with one service agency reporting $430,000 in possible monthly recurring deals over eight months, even if those deals haven't closed yet.

If you adjust your online ads smartly, spending more money can lead to significantly more people signing up for your service, as one company saw 134% more sign-ups when they increased their ad investment.
question: The article shows how different online advertising methods, like Google Search or social media ads, can lead to various outcomes, from "potential monthly recurring deal value" to "qualified leads" or "trial registrations." How might understanding that these different approaches yield different types of results change how you would measure success or decide where to invest your efforts in attracting new interest for your own projects or business?
